column1: # How people actually type Assamese in Latin letters, and what they mean by it.
# The Assamese phonetic layout runs the Bangla Avro rules, reads a typed "x" as
# "s" and turns every র into ৰ, so this list holds the spellings that pipeline
#  - Chat romanization writes চ and ছ as "s" ("ase" is আছে, "kisu" কিছু,
#    "xohor" চহৰ), so the rules land on স.
#  - The o-sound is written "u" or "o" and the rules hear neither as ো: "mur" /
#    "mor" is মোৰ, "tumar" তোমাৰ, "kunu" কোনো. The same goes for the ' of the
#    short forms ("hol" হ'ল, "kot" ক'ত, "kobo" ক'ব), for ৱ ("kua" কোৱা,
#    "suwali" ছোৱালী) and for the nasal of the first person ("asu" আছোঁ,
#  - Chat shorthand that drops letters wholesale: "tmr" for তোমাৰ, "kn" for
#  - A handful of everyday words the rules already spell right (মই, তুমি,
#    আৰু, কি …) are here too, because Assamese ships no bundled word list and
#    until the user downloads one these lines are all the vocabulary the layout
# A hand-written draft of the commonest few hundred chat words; it wants an
# Assamese speaker's review. Every value was checked against the Assamese word
# list in wmkeyboard-data (data/as/as_full.txt.gz). That list is encyclopedic
# prose, so a few colloquial verb forms (খালোঁ, খাইছা, গৈছোঁ, ক'বা …) are
# missing from it and are kept here on the strength of standard spelling.
# Format: spelling<TAB>assamese   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# A spelling may repeat to offer several forms, most-preferred first.
# Loaded after en_as.tsv, so the hand-written loanword spellings win a tie.
